notes: No release before 0.5.0 may claim any of this is balanced: every magnitude in the shipped content carries tuningStatus untuned and the balance harness owns all of them -- so this file is a measurement and not a balance claim.

The universe is still degenerate in the following ways, and this edit closes two of them and withdraws two statements the superseded files made. The fast and horizon sweeps are 100 percent passive-control and submit no god verb; the ascension sweep round-robins all eight strategies, which is the one place a strategy is exercised at all, and the superseded files called all three passive. Scribing no longer stops for good when the stock empties: the single materials pool is now food, stone and vellum and a scribe spends only vellum, so over the reference two hundred years the final twenty-year window scribes 5 books where it used to scribe none. Portals now open. The superseded files say nothing in packages/scenario opens one and that no raid runs in any committed sweep, and that is no longer true: raids.ts installs the arrival process and drives rules-raid to termination, and the executor declares raidEngagement true by default. Teaching does not die out either -- but the superseded files' statement that a lesson is taught in every one of the ten twenty-year windows, the thinnest holding 16, is withdrawn as false. It held for one run seed. Three of five seeds violate it on the tree those files were measured on, and three of five violate it here. Teaching supply oscillates and a two-hundred-year horizon can end inside a trough; packages/scenario/test/unit/reference-long-run.test.ts carries the seeds, the per-window supply counts and the three explanations they rule out.

knowledgeKind has no consumer in the rules path. When metis-knowledge is implemented, scribing refusal and succession loss will change these numbers for real, and that regeneration will be a behaviour claim in a way this one is not.

The three notes above are carried forward verbatim from the superseded file. This regeneration makes no claim about any of them: the regeneration command replaces `notes` wholesale when --note is not passed, which has silently dropped the 0.5.0 disclaimer before, so they are re-passed through the sealing path rather than hand-edited back in afterwards -- contentHash is a digest over every field including these, and a hand patch would break the file's own integrity guard.

Two other branches are re-recording these same three files. When this branch and those are merged, the three baselines want re-recording ONCE from the merged tree rather than hand-merging three sets of numbers against each other -- which is the mistake d5a3357 records having made and then corrected.
rationale:
Displacement authored on five effects, and the reason this file is being rewritten is the content digest and not a metric. 6973d2c55f6d7788bbaa6886e507bbde -> 5ab771101485e49068f7f94648fa2bc3: node.json's effect schema gained an optional `displacement` term, and five effects on the four rego-terram nodes carry one. 296 of the 300 nodes carry none and are byte-identical. No other content file changed. EVERY METRIC IN THIS FILE PASSED ITS TOLERANCE BEFORE THIS REGENERATION. The gate's refusal was `baseline-invalid: provenance.contentHash`, which is a category error the gate is right to raise and not a regression -- it compares two runs of one build, and this is two builds. The three gate runs against the superseded file are recorded in PR #79 and can be reproduced by checking out this branch, restoring the superseded baselines and running the three gate scripts. No tolerance was widened and no --tolerance-k flag was passed: k is 3 here and was 3 in the superseded file. No constant, cap or magnitude was tuned to produce any movement below; the only edit is the authored content and the mechanism that reads it. 

At two hundred world years, with all eight strategies round-robined, displacement costs a third of the books. referenceGrimoires 283.5625 -> 184.15625 (-99.40625, -2.24 SE) is the movement worth stating as a behavioural claim rather than as an in-tolerance number: over two centuries the labour that displacement removes is labour that would have made vellum, and a universe that quarries without hands writes down a third less of what it knows. referencePeakPopulation 29490 -> 27703 (-1787, -0.93 SE) and referencePopulation 15732.25 -> 15098.25 (-634, -0.44 SE) move the same way and are not significant. referenceLibraryDepth 34.125 -> 31.34375 (-2.78, -0.42 SE) and referenceLivingMages 459.875 -> 447.4375 (-12.44, -0.07 SE) likewise. What did not move is knowledge: referenceNodesKnown 60.875 -> 61.03125 and referenceNodesGained 58.375 -> 58.53125 are 0.01 SE, and referenceNodesGainedFinalQuarter 4.875 -> 5.40625 is 0.25 SE. Displacement costs a universe what it has and what it writes down, not what it knows -- which is the same shape the horizon file reports from twenty years away, and the opposite face of the same content ceiling. The tolerances here are wide (133.35 on referenceGrimoires against a 99.41 delta) because 32 runs at two hundred years is a noisy instrument, so 'passed tolerance' is a weaker statement in this file than in the other two. It is recorded as such rather than leaned on.
